overview: Mali connected West African gold-producing regions with a wider commercial and intellectual world. Mansa Musa became internationally famous through his pilgrimage, while architecture and oral performance preserved different forms of cultural memory.

items.text: Gold and salt served long-distance commerce; cowrie shells also entered local exchange during the fourteenth century.
Mansa Musa passed through Cairo during his pilgrimage in 1324 to 1325. His distribution of gold made a strong impression on contemporaries.
Timbuktu's Djingareyber Mosque traces its initial construction to Musa's return from pilgrimage. Later rebuilding means the surviving fabric represents multiple periods.
Mande jeliw transmit historical epics through skilled performance. Musical accompaniment helps structure and pace narratives.
Mosque architecture and scholarship connected Timbuktu to Islamic networks while local building practices remained central.
